novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanistic relationship, namely that “benign, task-irrelevant surrounding context” contaminates a model's “pre-generation difficulty representation” and thereby inflates reasoning compute, rather than merely studying long-context performance. The closest prior work is *Probing the Difficulty Perception Mechanism of Large Language Models* (2025), which identifies linearly encoded difficulty and difficulty-sensitive heads, alongside *Evaluating Long-Context Reasoning in LLM-Based WebAgents* (2025), which reports degradation from irrelevant inserted histories; searches using “LLM difficulty perception irrelevant context,” “benign context reasoning token inflation,” “difficulty representation distractor reasoning,” and “irrelevant context adaptive compute” did not reveal an essentially equivalent study. The step from these works to the claim requires a new core relationship—benign context complexity specifically shifting the difficulty estimate and causing excess reasoning—although the proposed reset uses standard probing and activation-steering principles, so this is high novelty within the established framework rather than a paradigm-level advance.
